title: Globalisation & TNCs
examples: How does a big company affect a local town?
What are the good and bad things about TNCs?
Can TNCs really help or hurt a country?

explain.say: Today we explore how large companies operate globally.

items: Their impact is both positive and negative.

explain.say: First we look at the economic flows TNCs create.
These companies often bring jobs and new technology to areas.
However, TNCs can sometimes cause pollution in local areas.
Think about a large shoe company setting up a factory.
In everyday life, think about your phone's journey to you.

faq.q: Do TNCs always make money for the home country?
faq.a: Not always. Sometimes they keep profits in their home country, which can limit local benefit.
asks: Where does the money go from TNCs?
Do TNCs take all the profit?

faq.q: What is meant by 'resource depletion' from TNCs?
faq.a: It means that the company uses up natural resources faster than they can naturally replace themselves.

faq.q: Are TNCs always bad for the environment?
faq.a: No, some TNCs invest in green technology, but they can cause pollution through waste.

faq.q: Does globalisation mean all countries are the same?
faq.a: No, it means they are more connected, but local cultures and economies can still remain different.
asks: What is the effect of globalisation?

faq.q: What is the difference between local and TNC impact?
faq.a: Local impact is seen in one town; TNC impact is felt across many national borders.
asks: Is TNC impact bigger than local impact?
How do I compare the two impacts?

faq.q: What should governments do to control TNCs?
faq.a: Governments can set strict environmental laws and tax rules for these large companies.

faq.q: What is the main economic flow shown by TNCs?
faq.a: The main flow is the movement of capital and goods across international borders.

facts: TNCs operate in more than one country.
They often establish supply chains across continents.
Positive impacts include job creation and infrastructure building.
Negative impacts include pollution and exploitation of labour.

quiz.say: A TNC builds a new road and hospital in a developing country. This is an example of:
quiz.why: Building roads and hospitals directly creates employment and improves local facilities.

wrong.0: This is an accounting term about money leaving the country.
wrong.2: This suggests using up natural materials, not building things.
wrong.3: This refers to too much product, not the building of facilities.

quiz.say: If a TNC pollutes a river, this is an example of:
quiz.why: Pollution is the introduction of harmful substances into the environment.

wrong.0: Capital flow is about money moving, not pollution.
wrong.1: Export growth is a positive economic measure.
wrong.2: This measures profit, not environmental damage.

quiz.say: When a TNC designs a product in one country and makes it in another, this process is best described as:
quiz.why: The division of labour means different parts of the process happen in different places.

wrong.0: This means needing nothing from outside, which is the opposite.
wrong.1: Barter uses goods directly, not complex global chains.
wrong.3: Localisation means staying in one place, not moving across borders.
